## Coming soon

These How-Tos are on the way. Each will stand on its own, like the ones already
listed on the [How-Tos](howtos.qmd) page.

## Using your own data

The bridge from the practice datasets to a file of your own: opening an Excel,
CSV, or commercial-software file, keeping it in a data folder, and taking a first
look with `jscreen()`.

## Working with data from commercial statistical software

Importing and working with data from SPSS, Stata, and SAS, including value and
variable labels and the different missing-value conventions.

## Reading jstats output: Case Processing and Missing data

Not how to interpret the statistics, but how to read the accounting printed above
them: the Case Processing lines and tables that say how many cases an analysis
used and which were set aside, and the Missing data breakdown that shows where
each variable's missing values went.

## Recoding and relabeling variables

Reverse-coding an item, collapsing categories, and fixing variable and value
labels with `jrecode()` and `jrelabel()`, keeping the original column intact.

## Text answers into coded variables

Turning a column of words ("Yes", "No", "Don't know") from a spreadsheet or survey
export into a labeled, coded variable with `jencode()`.

## Building and checking a scale

Combining Likert items into a scale and checking its reliability with Cronbach's
alpha.

## Working on part of your data

Analyzing a subgroup with `jsubset()`, and using `jcomplete()` so a set of
analyses all run on the same cases.

## Comparing groups: t-tests and cross-tabulations

t-tests with `jt()` and cross-tabulations with `jcrosstab()`: the same formula
style as `jaov()`, how to read what comes back, and the Welch version of the
t-test (`welch = TRUE`), which does not assume equal variances.
[One-way ANOVA](anova.qmd) is already available.

## Regression with categorical predictors

Linear and logistic regression with `jlm()` and `jlogistic()`. `jdummy()` is the
quick way in for a categorical variable: register its dummy coding and reference
category once, and it goes into a model by name — no building dummy variables by
hand, and no converting to base R's factors.

## Handling missing values across platforms

What survives when data move between SPSS, Stata, SAS, and R: round trips between
formats, converting declarations from one convention to another, missing-value
ranges, and the SAS interchange format. Declaring missing values in the first
place is covered in
*[Telling jstats about missing values](missing-values.qmd)*.
